Inside ChatGPT, there are no words. Only long lists of numbers. So how does it follow grammar?
In 1884, Georges Seurat painted a Paris park out of thousands of tiny dots.
Up close, one dot means nothing. Step back, and a whole Sunday afternoon appears.
Yale linguist Tom McCoy and colleagues think language models may work the same way.
They replaced the numbers inside seven large models with roles and fillers. In 'cats chase dogs', the words fill the roles of subject, verb, and object.
The models' behavior barely changed. And editing one role made a model read 'the clever doctor' as 'the clever lawyer'.
It's a preprint, and McCoy says it only scratches the surface.
